paper: Sim et al. 2019, Multipolar superconductivity in Luttinger semimetals (arXiv:1911.13224)

open_questions.question: What is the sign of the Ginzburg-Landau quartic invariant q2 for the eg doublet in the exact one-loop / two-band-projected-gap treatment, and why does a single-gap BdG condensation-energy proxy give the opposite sign?
open_questions.why_it_matters: q2>0 is the entire content of the headline claim (TR-breaking (1,i) selected). Our proxy gives q2<0. Nailing the sign from the correct microscopic quartic coefficient is the difference between confirming and contradicting the paper's central result.
open_questions.next_step: Derive q2 analytically via the one-loop particle-particle bubble with the eg vertices M1,M2 projected onto the two active Luttinger bands at E_F (Boettcher-Herbut PRL 120,057002 SI method), and compare to a fully self-consistent multi-gap BdG free-energy minimization rather than a fixed-Delta condensation energy.

open_questions.question: Does the self-consistently determined gap magnitude Delta_a(k) (solving the full nonlinear gap equation) change the state ordering relative to the fixed-Delta condensation-energy comparison used here?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The TR-breaking state may have a larger self-consistent Delta (it fully gaps most of the FS) that overcompensates the pocket cost. A fixed-Delta comparison cannot see this; only a self-consistent solve can.
open_questions.next_step: Implement the coupled self-consistency Delta_a = g <psi^T gamma45 gamma_a psi> at each temperature, iterate to convergence per candidate state, and compare converged free energies F[Delta_a*].

open_questions.question: Do the 16 Bogoliubov Fermi-surface pockets of the (1,i) state carry Chern numbers +/-2 as claimed (Class D + inversion, 2Z classification)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the topological headline that makes the state a topological superconductor; it is an independent, falsifiable prediction not touched by the energetics.
open_questions.next_step: For the (1,i) BdG Hamiltonian, locate the gapless pockets, wrap a small BZ sphere around each, and compute the Chern number by the standard Fukui-Hatsugai-Suzuki lattice-plaquette Berry-flux method.

open_questions.question: How does the ferro-quadrupolar order <O20> reshape the phase diagram (Fig.1) — specifically the transition from eg (1,i) to the t2g dyz+idzx (1,i) state via Fermi-surface distortion c3=c4=(-1-J_K<O20>)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The paper's central novelty is that multipolar order tunes the SC channel and thus the topology. Reproducing the phase boundary would validate the quadrupolar-Kondo mechanism, not just the cubic column.
open_questions.next_step: Scan J_K<O20> in [0,1.5] and g, recomputing Part A/B with the distorted c_eta, and map which channel (eg vs eta=(d3,d4)) has the leading instability at each point.

open_questions.question: Is the microscopic projected Kondo coupling (Eq.7) correctly derived from the orbital form factors Gamma^a_{1,ij}, Gamma^a_{2,ij}, and does it reproduce the stated c3=c4!=c5 anisotropy quantitatively?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Eq.7 is the bridge from the localized Pr quadrupoles to the itinerant Fermi-surface distortion; the whole quadrupolar-Kondo story rests on it. We assumed the renormalized c-coefficients rather than deriving them.
open_questions.next_step: Reconstruct the two-FCC-sublattice tight-binding form factors from SI Sec.II, apply the j=3/2 projector P, and verify the resulting H_K(k) matches Eq.7 term-by-term.
